html:
An altar to Peace in Rome, voted by the Senate in 13 BCE to mark Augustus's return from Spain and Gaul, and dedicated in 9 BCE. It stood on the Campus Martius beside the road north out of the city.

The altar sits inside a marble enclosure carved with some of the finest reliefs of Roman art. Long panels show a procession of the imperial family, with Augustus, Agrippa, Livia and small children holding their parents' clothes. Other panels show Aeneas making a sacrifice, as in the Aeneid, and a mother goddess with babies, animals and plants, a picture of the plenty that the Pax Romana promised. Lower down run scrolls of acanthus leaves full of tiny creatures.

The altar was later buried under river silt. Pieces turned up from the 1500s on, and in 1938 Mussolini had it dug out and rebuilt beside the Mausoleum of Augustus to celebrate his own new Roman empire. Since 2006 it has stood in a museum designed by Richard Meier.
sum: An altar to Peace in Rome, voted by the Senate in 13 BCE to mark Augustus's return from Spain and Gaul, and dedicated in 9 BCE. It stood on the Campus Martius beside the road north out of the city.
